  • Quantile Regression Forests vs. Gradient Boosting

Quantile Regression Forests vs. Gradient Boosting#

This example compares the quantiles predicted by a quantile regression forest (QRF) with those predicted by gradient boosting. Gradient boosting fits a separate model for each quantile, whereas a QRF fits one model and predicts every quantile from the same estimated distribution. Both predict 19 quantiles, from 5% to 95%, shown here as a fan of prediction intervals. Because the gradient boosting models are fit independently, their quantiles can cross, with a higher quantile predicted below a lower one (marked in red), which no distribution allows. The quantiles of a QRF cannot cross, and a QRF can predict any other quantile without being refit. Use the slider to select an X, at which the panels below plot each model’s predicted quantiles: those of the QRF never decrease, whereas those of gradient boosting decrease wherever they cross.

import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
from sklearn.metrics import mean_pinball_loss
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.utils.validation import check_random_state

from quantile_forest import RandomForestQuantileRegressor

random_state = np.random.RandomState(0)
n_samples = 1000
bounds = [0, 10]
quantiles = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, num=19).round(2).tolist()  # in steps of 0.05
coverage = quantiles[-1] - quantiles[0]  # the target coverage of the widest interval


def make_toy_dataset(n_samples, bounds, random_state=None):
    """Make a toy dataset with right-skewed noise that grows with x."""
    random_state = check_random_state(random_state)

    x = random_state.uniform(*bounds, size=n_samples)
    f = 3 * np.sin(x)

    sigma = 0.25 + x / 20
    noise = random_state.lognormal(sigma=sigma) - np.exp(sigma**2 / 2)
    y = f + noise

    return np.atleast_2d(x).T, y


X, y = make_toy_dataset(n_samples, bounds, random_state=random_state)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, random_state=random_state)

# A QRF is fit once, and can then predict any quantile.
qrf = RandomForestQuantileRegressor(min_samples_leaf=10, random_state=random_state)
qrf.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Gradient boosting is fit once for each quantile.
gbms = [
    HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss="quantile", quantile=q, random_state=random_state)
    for q in quantiles
]
for gbm in gbms:
    gbm.fit(X_train, y_train)

models = {
    "QRF (1 Model)": lambda X: qrf.predict(X, quantiles=quantiles),
    f"Gradient Boosting ({len(gbms)} Models)": lambda X: np.column_stack(
        [gbm.predict(X) for gbm in gbms]
    ),
}


def is_crossed(y_pred):
    """Get whether each adjacent pair of predicted quantiles of each sample crosses."""
    return np.diff(y_pred, axis=1) < 0


def get_crossed(model, X, y_pred):
    """Get the adjacent pairs of predicted quantiles that cross, for each sample."""
    # Each crossing spans the predictions of an adjacent pair of quantiles.
    rows, cols = np.nonzero(is_crossed(y_pred))
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "model": model,
            "x": X[rows, 0],
            "quantile_low": np.array(quantiles)[cols],
            "quantile_upp": np.array(quantiles)[cols + 1],
            "y_pred_low": y_pred[rows, cols],
            "y_pred_upp": y_pred[rows, cols + 1],
        }
    )


# Evaluate the predictions on the test data, predict on evenly spaced inputs,
# and predict on the inputs that can be selected, in steps of 0.2.
X_grid = np.linspace(*bounds, num=300).reshape(-1, 1)
X_select = np.linspace(*bounds, num=51).round(1).reshape(-1, 1)
metrics, dfs_intervals, dfs_median, dfs_crossed = {}, [], [], []
dfs_quantiles, dfs_crossed_select = [], []
for name, predict in models.items():
    y_pred_test = predict(X_test)
    metrics[name] = {
        "crossed": np.mean(np.any(is_crossed(y_pred_test), axis=1)),
        "pinball_loss": np.mean(
            [
                mean_pinball_loss(y_test, y_pred_test[:, i], alpha=q)
                for i, q in enumerate(quantiles)
            ]
        ),
        "coverage": np.mean((y_pred_test[:, 0] <= y_test) & (y_test <= y_pred_test[:, -1])),
    }

    y_pred = predict(X_grid)

    # The fan of intervals between each quantile and its mirror (5% to 95%, 10% to 90%, ...).
    for i in range(len(quantiles) // 2):
        dfs_intervals.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "model": name,
                    "x": X_grid[:, 0],
                    "interval": f"{quantiles[i]:.0%} to {quantiles[-1 - i]:.0%}",
                    "y_pred_low": y_pred[:, i],
                    "y_pred_upp": y_pred[:, -1 - i],
                }
            )
        )

    dfs_median.append(
        pd.DataFrame({"model": name, "x": X_grid[:, 0], "y_pred": y_pred[:, quantiles.index(0.5)]})
    )
    dfs_crossed.append(get_crossed(name, X_grid, y_pred))

    # The predicted quantiles at each input that can be selected.
    y_pred_select = predict(X_select)
    for i, q in enumerate(quantiles):
        dfs_quantiles.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "model": name,
                    "x": X_select[:, 0],
                    "quantile": q,
                    "y_pred": y_pred_select[:, i],
                }
            )
        )
    dfs_crossed_select.append(get_crossed(name, X_select, y_pred_select))

df_test = pd.DataFrame({"x": X_test[:, 0], "y": y_test})
df_intervals = pd.concat(dfs_intervals, ignore_index=True)
df_median = pd.concat(dfs_median, ignore_index=True)
df_crossed = pd.concat(dfs_crossed, ignore_index=True)
df_quantiles = pd.concat(dfs_quantiles, ignore_index=True)
df_crossed_select = pd.concat(dfs_crossed_select, ignore_index=True)

# Start at the selectable input where the gradient boosting quantiles cross the most.
gbm_name = list(models)[1]
y_pred_gbm = df_quantiles.query("model == @gbm_name").pivot(
    index="x", columns="quantile", values="y_pred"
)
x_start = y_pred_gbm.index[np.diff(y_pred_gbm.to_numpy(), axis=1).min(axis=1).argmin()]


def plot_quantile_fans(
    df_test, df_intervals, df_median, df_crossed, df_quantiles, df_crossed_select, metrics
):
    """Plot the fan of predicted quantiles of each model, with its crossings."""
    colors = {
        "Test Observations": "#f2a619",
        "Predicted Median": "#006aff",
        f"Predicted Quantiles ({quantiles[0]:.0%} to {quantiles[-1]:.0%})": "#99c2ff",
        "Crossed Quantiles": "red",
    }
    labels = list(colors.keys())
    # The legend symbols. The median is drawn as a thin bar rather than a stroke, as
    # stroked symbols would space the legend entries unevenly, and the crossings,
    # which are vertical segments, as a thin vertical bar.
    bar = "M-1,-0.2L1,-0.2L1,0.2L-1,0.2Z"
    vertical_bar = "M-0.2,-1L0.2,-1L0.2,1L-0.2,1Z"
    shapes = ["circle", bar, "circle", vertical_bar]

    # Slider for selecting the input at which the predicted quantiles are plotted.
    slider = alt.binding_range(name="Selected X: ", min=bounds[0], max=bounds[1], step=0.2)
    x_val = alt.param(name="x_value", value=x_start, bind=slider)

    filter_x = "round(datum.x * 5) == round(x_value * 5)"

    # Clicking an entry of the legend highlights its marks (shift-click for more).
    click = alt.selection_point(name="click", fields=["label"], bind="legend")

    def _opacity(value, faded=0.1):
        return alt.condition(click, alt.value(value), alt.value(faded))

    x = alt.X("x:Q", scale=alt.Scale(domain=bounds, nice=False), title="X")
    y_scale = alt.Scale(domain=[-4, 8])

    def _plot_panel(model, legend=False):
        circle_test = (
            alt.Chart(df_test.assign(label=labels[0]))
            .mark_circle(clip=True, color=colors[labels[0]], size=15)
            .encode(
                x=x,
                y=alt.Y("y:Q", scale=y_scale, title="Y"),
                opacity=_opacity(0.6),
                tooltip=[
                    alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y:Q", format=",.3f", title="Y"),
                ],
            )
        )

        # The intervals are drawn translucently, so that the fan darkens toward its middle.
        areas_intervals = (
            alt.Chart(df_intervals.query("model == @model").assign(label=labels[2]))
            .mark_area(color="#006aff")
            .encode(
                x=x,
                y="y_pred_low:Q",
                y2="y_pred_upp:Q",
                detail="interval:N",
                opacity=_opacity(0.12, faded=0.02),
                tooltip=[
                    alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                    alt.Tooltip("interval:N", title="Quantiles"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y_pred_low:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Lower Y"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y_pred_upp:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Upper Y"),
                ],
            )
        )

        line_median = (
            alt.Chart(df_median.query("model == @model").assign(label=labels[1]))
            .mark_line(color=colors[labels[1]], size=2)
            .encode(
                x=x,
                y="y_pred:Q",
                opacity=_opacity(1),
                tooltip=[
                    alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y_pred:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Median"),
                ],
            )
        )

        rules_crossed = (
            alt.Chart(df_crossed.query("model == @model").assign(label=labels[3]))
            .mark_rule(color=colors[labels[3]], size=2)
            .encode(
                x=x,
                y="y_pred_upp:Q",
                y2="y_pred_low:Q",
                opacity=_opacity(1),
                tooltip=[
                    alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.3f", title="X"),
                    alt.Tooltip("quantile_low:Q", format=".0%", title="Lower Quantile"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y_pred_low:Q", format=",.3f", title="Lower Quantile's Y"),
                    alt.Tooltip("quantile_upp:Q", format=".0%", title="Upper Quantile"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y_pred_upp:Q", format=",.3f", title="Upper Quantile's Y"),
                ],
            )
        )

        # Mark the selected input, below the metrics.
        rule_selected = (
            alt.Chart(df_quantiles.query("model == @model & quantile == 0.5"))
            .transform_filter(filter_x)
            .mark_rule(color="gray", strokeDash=[4, 4])
            .encode(x="x:Q", y=alt.datum(-4), y2=alt.datum(5.5))
        )

        text = "\n".join(
            [
                f"Crossed Quantiles: {metrics[model]['crossed']:.1%} of Samples",
                f"Mean Pinball Loss: {metrics[model]['pinball_loss']:.3f}",
                f"Coverage: {metrics[model]['coverage']:.1%} (target = {coverage:.0%})",
            ]
        )
        text_metrics = (
            alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"text": [text]}))
            .mark_text(align="left", baseline="top", color="gray", lineBreak="\n")
            .encode(x=alt.value(5), y=alt.value(5), text="text:N")
        )

        layers = [
            circle_test,
            areas_intervals,
            line_median,
            rules_crossed,
            rule_selected,
            text_metrics,
        ]
        if legend:
            # A legend of all of the marks, drawn by invisible points.
            scale = alt.Scale(domain=labels, range=list(colors.values()))
            layers.append(
                alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"label": labels}))
                .mark_point(filled=True, opacity=0)
                .encode(
                    color=alt.Color(
                        "label:N",
                        scale=scale,
                        legend=alt.Legend(symbolOpacity=1, rowPadding=5),
                        title=None,
                    ),
                    shape=alt.Shape(
                        "label:N", scale=alt.Scale(domain=labels, range=shapes), title=None
                    ),
                )
                .add_params(click)
            )
        return alt.layer(*layers).properties(title=model, height=250, width=280)

    def _plot_quantiles(model):
        x_quantile = alt.X(
            "quantile:Q",
            axis=alt.Axis(format="%"),
            scale=alt.Scale(domain=[0, 1], nice=False),
            title="Quantile",
        )
        # The y-axis zooms in on the quantiles at the selected X. It starts and ends on
        # a tick at every X, with the points kept clear of its ends, so that the panels
        # don't shift as the slider moves.
        y_quantile = alt.Y(
            "y_pred:Q",
            axis=alt.Axis(tickCount=4),
            scale=alt.Scale(nice=4, padding=6, zero=False),
            title="Y",
        )
        tooltip = [
            alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.1f", title="X"),
            alt.Tooltip("quantile:Q", format=".0%", title="Quantile"),
            alt.Tooltip("y_pred:Q", format=",.3f", title="Predicted Y"),
        ]

        line_quantiles = (
            alt.Chart(df_quantiles.query("model == @model").assign(label=labels[2]))
            .transform_filter(filter_x)
            .mark_line(color=colors[labels[2]], size=2)
            .encode(
                x=x_quantile,
                y=y_quantile,
                opacity=_opacity(1),
                tooltip=tooltip,
            )
        )

        circles_quantiles = (
            alt.Chart(df_quantiles.query("model == @model").assign(label=labels[2]))
            .transform_filter(filter_x)
            .mark_circle(color=colors[labels[2]], size=30)
            .encode(x=x_quantile, y="y_pred:Q", opacity=_opacity(1), tooltip=tooltip)
        )

        circle_median = (
            alt.Chart(
                df_quantiles.query("model == @model & quantile == 0.5").assign(label=labels[1])
            )
            .transform_filter(filter_x)
            .mark_circle(color=colors[labels[1]], size=75)
            .encode(x=x_quantile, y="y_pred:Q", opacity=_opacity(1), tooltip=tooltip)
        )

        # Each crossing is drawn from the lower quantile's prediction to the upper one's.
        rules_crossed = (
            alt.Chart(df_crossed_select.query("model == @model").assign(label=labels[3]))
            .transform_filter(filter_x)
            .mark_rule(color=colors[labels[3]], size=2)
            .encode(
                x="quantile_low:Q",
                x2="quantile_upp:Q",
                y="y_pred_low:Q",
                y2="y_pred_upp:Q",
                opacity=_opacity(1),
                tooltip=[
                    alt.Tooltip("x:Q", format=",.1f", title="X"),
                    alt.Tooltip("quantile_low:Q", format=".0%", title="Lower Quantile"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y_pred_low:Q", format=",.3f", title="Lower Quantile's Y"),
                    alt.Tooltip("quantile_upp:Q", format=".0%", title="Upper Quantile"),
                    alt.Tooltip("y_pred_upp:Q", format=",.3f", title="Upper Quantile's Y"),
                ],
            )
        )

        title = f"{model.split(' (')[0]} Quantiles at the Selected X"
        layers = [line_quantiles, circles_quantiles, rules_crossed, circle_median]
        return alt.layer(*layers).properties(title=title, height=150, width=280)

    qrf_name, gbm_name = metrics.keys()
    # Space the panels a little closer than by default, so that the chart fits the width
    # of the documentation.
    row_fans = alt.hconcat(_plot_panel(qrf_name), _plot_panel(gbm_name, legend=True), spacing=12)
    row_quantiles = alt.hconcat(_plot_quantiles(qrf_name), _plot_quantiles(gbm_name), spacing=12)

    # Give every y-axis the width of the widest labels, so that the panels stay aligned,
    # and in place, as the labels of the quantile panels change with the selected input.
    chart = (
        alt.vconcat(row_fans, row_quantiles.resolve_scale(y="shared"))
        .add_params(x_val)
        .configure_axisY(minExtent=27, maxExtent=27)
    )
    return chart


chart = plot_quantile_fans(
    df_test, df_intervals, df_median, df_crossed, df_quantiles, df_crossed_select, metrics
)
chart
